To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
, for medium-to-high SNRs, the optimal target transmit powers of the EH node are less than the average power harvested by the EH node and increase with the capacity of its energy buffer.
the optimal target transmit powers for the on-off policy are smaller than the average harvested powers and increase with the energy buffer capacity.

the optimal transmission policy is to transmit with a constant desired power when the energy buffer content is larger than the target power, otherwise to remain silent; and that the diversity order of a Rayleigh-faded uplink channel is not affected by a finite-capacity energy buffer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental tradeoff between the energy storage capacity and the performance of wireless powered communication systems.
a simple on-off transmission policy for the EH node, which can be implemented with low complexity and does not require any channel state information.
the design of practical transmission strategies and performance analysis for wireless powered communication networks with energy storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the on-off transmission policy, which is simple to implement, can achieve good performance.
, in the presence of a finite-size energy buffer, a simple transmission policy with constant target transmit power is optimal in terms of average error rate.
the optimal transmit power of the energy harvesting node increases with the energy buffer capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the on-off transmission policy is simple yet efficient in terms of energy efficiency, and the energy buffer capacity is an important design parameter.
, with a finite energy buffer, a wireless powered node should use a constant target transmit power which is less than the mean harvested power.

, with an energy harvesting node, the optimal transmit policy is to transmit with a constant power, which is less than the time average harvested power, and that the diversity order in the uplink is not affected by finite energy buffers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, even with the simple on-off transmission policy, the performance of the EH node in terms of average error rate and outage probability can be made arbitrarily close to that of an EH node with perfect knowledge of the EH process and the UL channel state.

, in order to achieve the optimal performance, the target transmit power should not be set too high, as this would require the EH node to store a large amount of energy in its energy buffer, which may be difficult to achieve.
a simple on-off policy can be optimal for wireless power transfer and EH.
